scope: Read-only original ROM and current accepted-source-compatible native runtime review; no tracked edits, no new acceptance claim.

findings.finding: A random key world is identified byCC44 bit7 plusCC42 cache slot,CC43 floor,CC45 structure/link and generatedCDxx descriptors. FF90 is the fixed-map byte and can remain stale. A fixed-world navigation/acceptance condition alone can silently name the wrong world.
findings.recommendation: Use context-sensitive original random observer and actual rendered/collision observations. Treat helper/decompressor mismatches as observer uncertainty until original runtime evidence establishes a game defect.

findings.finding: Original96:4001 first allocates a slot via6C61; cached data is cartridge-owned. SRAM bank2 holds20 records of0x195 bytes: marker50+slot and194 bytes fromCD07. 6CD1 restores onlymatching-marker records, CC42 must be<20. Full-slot exhaustion returnsFF. A single key entry does not test repeated entry, different keys, retirement, slot-full behavior or restoration.
findings.recommendation: Prioritize real same-key exit/re-entry, actual Journal/new Runtime Continue, a second genuine key, and cache-byte/descriptor observations.20-slot exhaustion is a separate optional bounded stress case; do not fabricate keys or edit caches.

findings.finding: Existing native Session::verify_continue comparesC6FD..<C82D, CBD7..<CC0F (56 quest bytes), fixedFF90/8F/92/8E/91 and22 persistent bytes per active party member. It does not itself check flags206/207 atCC17, generated contextCC42.., whole cache persistence, or all farm creatures. The original main-story Python verifier separately covered107 quest bytes and every owned creature.
findings.recommendation: Retain existing fail-closed guards; supplement observational comparisons of107 quest bytes, all original owned records and generated descriptors/cache/revisited layouts. Do not equate native Journal PASS with complete postgame persistence.

findings.finding: DWM2T_ALL_ROMX translates all255 ROMX banks and every16384 byte offset in4 chunks, not just known branch entry points. This avoids a missing-bank gap for new generator paths, but does not prove every original opcode/timing path or every procedural recipe has been exercised. Runtime traps execution outside ROM apart from known HRAM DMA; newly reached dynamic RAM code would fail closed.
findings.recommendation: Keep exact f93 full-AOT binary unchanged for new samples; retain raw runtime traps if any. New procedural maps should be produced by original ROM96/97, never host replacements. Test semantic outcomes, not only bank inclusion.

findings.finding: M8 per-frame instruction budget, per-command frame budgets and host scripts are operational limits. Existing talk/battle convenience commands pulseA and can choose defaults; earlier story direct-skill helper assumes a manual command menu. The post-ending granddaughter Arena battle actually exposes tactics-only menus. These helpers can fail or play poorly without a native game defect. Journal requires idle field and an empty facing tile; pending postbattle dialogue must finish first.
findings.recommendation: Inspect original menus/choices, preserve every failed attempt, distinguish host-budget/selection failures from original runtime traps, and use deliberateP1 for recruitment/name/skill decisions.

findings.finding: The memory model handles FF01/FF02 through generic IO storage; no serial-peer transport or serial-transfer ticking implementation was found in runtime/memory. Original serial interrupt vector exists, which is not proof of actual linked gameplay. Counterpart-only Baffle/Lonely and arrival text must not be reported as solo-tested content.
findings.recommendation: State single-P1 scope. A real original linked peer plus implemented transport and an actual witnessed exchange are prerequisites to claim these paths, without flags/keys substitution.

observed_other_session_caveat: Existing root observer comparison had unsupported-submode mismatches; those are not proof of a game defect and root owns current random-world gameplay.
